item.title: Antiviral effects of traditional herbal medicine Otsu-Ji-To against human coronavirus OC43, SARS-CoV-2, and its variants: in vitro and in vivo studies
item.description: BACKGROUND AND AIM: Otsu-Ji-To (OJT), also known as Eul-ja-tang in Korean, is a traditional herbal formula used to treat hemorrhoids. We investigated its antiviral effects against HCoV-OC43, SARS-CoV-2, and its variants.

item.title: Integrated computational screening and biochemical validation identify natural small molecules targeting Aβ aggregation and dissociation
item.description: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by the accumulation of amyloid-β (Aβ), a pathological hallmark implicated in disease onset and progression. Aβ undergoes self-assembly from monomers into soluble oligomers, protofibrils, insoluble fibrils, and extracellular plaques. Our previous studies have shown that Jowiseungchungtang, which consists of 14 medicinal herbs, inhibits Aβ aggregation and ameliorates Aβ-mediated pathology in AD models. However, the active small molecules underlying these...

item.title: Spatial and Seasonal Structuring of Bacterial Communities and Putative Pathogen-Associated Bacterial Taxa at Four Korean Coastal Locations
item.description: Coastal marine environments are dynamic transition zones where offshore water masses and terrestrial inputs shape microbial community structure. However, standardized comparisons of bacterial communities across geographically distinct Korean coastal waters remain limited, constraining the development of microbial baselines for long-term monitoring. Surface seawater bacterial communities from four Korean coastal locations were analysed using 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing. Total bacterial...

item.title: Glycol chitosan thermogels: a versatile platform for advanced drug delivery
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Injectable thermogels are promising localized drug delivery platforms as their temperature-triggered in situ gelation facilitates practical administration. However, conventional systems suffer from high critical gelation concentrations, limited biodegradability, cytotoxicity, or acidic degradation, which can cause local inflammation. Glycol chitosan (GC)-based thermogels have emerged as a promising alternative, combining aqueous solubility at physiological pH, biodegradability,...

item.title: Assessing the Age-Specific Seroepidemiology of Varicella-Zoster Virus in Korea in the Post-COVID-19 Era Using an Acetone-Fixed Cell FAMA Assay
item.description: CONCLUSION: This trend appears to partially reflect the current VZV notification in 2024. High VZV notification has shifted from the 0-4-year group to the 10-14-year group, while in 5-9-year-olds remains high. These findings likely reflect the combined effects of post-coronavirus disease 2019 non-pharmaceutical interventions and an age shift related to primary vaccination. The consistent low seroprevalence observed in children aged 5-9 years may provide supportive evidence for considering the...

item.title: Elevated human epididymis protein 4 levels in chronic kidney disease compromise the accuracy of the risk of ovarian malignancy algorithm
item.description: The present study aimed to compare the diagnostic accuracy of the risk of ovarian malignancy algorithm (ROMA) for differentiating ovarian tumors in patients with and without chronic kidney disease (CKD), using postoperative histopathological findings as the reference standard among patients who underwent surgery after ROMA testing. The retrospective study included 1,122 patients, including 21 with CKD, who met the inclusion criteria and underwent surgery for ovarian tumors at Gangneung Asan...

item.title: Homologous and heterologous booster of COVID-19 vaccines: A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: To address waves of SARS-CoV-2 infections caused by various variants of concern (VOC), experts have recommended heterologous booster vaccination as a strategy to enhance long-term immunity. Therefore, this study aimed to review available data from randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to compare the relative efficacy and safety of heterologous booster vaccines versus homologous booster vaccines. We conducted a comprehensive search of relevant studies up to July 10, 2024 using PubMed, Embase, Web...

item.title: EEG emotion-recognition datasets for neuroarchitecture: an appraisal of openness, AI-readiness and ontology maturity
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Neuroarchitecture studies how designed space shapes emotion, often with electroencephalography (EEG), and computational models that decode emotion from EEG must be trained on labelled recordings. Yet none of the widely shared EEG emotion datasets was recorded while people moved through designed spaces, and the few spatial recordings we found, all released since 2023, are single studies, each cited at most once. Researchers therefore borrow general emotion datasets, recorded from...

item.title: Socioeconomic inequalities in adolescent mental wellbeing in China-a longitudinal path analysis of sport opportunities, exercise self-efficacy, and physical activity
item.description: CONCLUSION: These findings are consistent with the proposition that higher socioeconomic status is associated with greater opportunities to participate in school and community sports, higher levels of exercise self-efficacy, higher rates of physical activity, and better later mental wellbeing. Because the design was observational and the Time 2 mediators were measured concurrently, these findings identify potentially modifiable correlates and plausible intervention targets rather than...

item.title: A deep learning approach for EPID-based patient-specific quality assurance incorporating daily machine-state variations
item.description: Patient-specific quality assurance (PSQA) based on electronic portal imaging devices (EPIDs) is widely used for pretreatment verification, but it is usually performed as a single check of the approved plan and reflects the daily state of the linac only to a limited extent. We propose a deep learning approach that predicts the measured EPID image from the calculated portal dose image using the daily machine state as a conditioning input. A Pix2Pix conditional generative adversarial network was...

item.title: Development of an Amplicon-Based Next-Generation Sequencing Assay for Pan-type Detection of BCR::ABL1 Kinase Domain Mutations
item.description: BCR::ABL1 kinase domain (KD) mutations confer tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) resistance in Philadelphia chromosome-positive (Ph+) leukemia, but conventional Sanger sequencing (SS) has limited sensitivity and most next-generation sequencing (NGS) assays cover only a single transcript type. We developed an amplicon-based NGS assay designed for pan-type amplification of major, minor, and micro BCR::ABL1 fusion transcript types, together with the entire KD, in a single multiplex long-range PCR. In...

item.title: Incremental Yield of CD34-Positive Cell Enrichment for Next-Generation Sequencing-Based Measurable Residual Disease Detection in CD34-Positive Acute Myeloid Leukemia
item.description: Next-generation sequencing (NGS)-based measurable residual disease (MRD) detection in AML may be limited by non-leukemic hematopoietic cells in bulk bone marrow samples. To address this limitation, we aimed to evaluate whether CD34-positive cell enrichment improves the detectability of residual variants. Paired MRD analyses were performed using unsorted and CD34-enriched bone marrow samples from patients with CD34-positive AML, tracking leukemia-associated variants identified at diagnosis in...

item.title: History and Future of Efficient Design of Quality Control in Clinical Laboratories
item.description: After half a century of development, conventional quality control (QC) theory has begun to approach its practical limits. Classical theories, including power function analysis, multi-rules, and patient risk models, have pushed conventional QC to its near-maximal efficiency. This review discusses this historical development and explores how patient-based real-time QC (PBRTQC) can theoretically drive future improvements in the information age. We focus on the key, yet often overlooked, concept of...

item.title: Three-Year Real-World Outcomes of Switching to Brolucizumab for Refractory Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Switching to brolucizumab provided maintained visual and anatomical improvements with extended treatment intervals over 3 years. The safety profile was consistent with previous reports, and IOI events were manageable in a real-world setting.

item.title: Loss of the Steep-Axis Flattening Effect in Sutured Clear Corneal Incisions: A Single-Surgeon Vector Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In this single-surgeon series of sutured clear corneal incisions, steep-axis incisions did not produce the expected flattening of the incision meridian, and the SIA acted predominantly as torque with a mean steepening effect. Whether the routine suture contributes to this pattern remains to be confirmed by direct sutured-versus-sutureless comparison.

item.title: The Reporting-Service Gap in Intimate Partner Violence: Police Reporting, Victim-Service Receipt, and Dual Noncontact in the National Crime Victimization Survey, 1993-2023
item.description: Research on intimate partner violence (IPV) underreporting often treats police notification as the primary indicator of formal-system reach, leaving less clear whether incidents not reported to police include recorded receipt of help or advice from victim-service agencies. Using incident-level public-use data from the National Crime Victimization Survey (NCVS), 1993 to 2023, this study examines the joint distribution of police reporting and receipt of victim-service help or advice among IPV...

item.title: Development and Psychometric Validation of the Korean Version of the Velopharyngeal Insufficiency Effects on Life Outcomes
item.description: ObjectiveTo develop and validate a culturally adapted Korean version of the Velopharyngeal Insufficiency Effects on Life Outcomes (K-VELO) for children with cleft palate with or without cleft lip (CP ± L).DesignMethodological study including linguistic validation and psychometric evaluation.Setting: Tertiary cleft centers in South Korea.Participants: A total of 74 children and 78 parents completed the K-VELO; 72 children and 62 parents also completed perceptual speech evaluations. For...

item.title: Assessment of health and nutrition issues and strategic directions for tailored nutrition management in a rural area of Gangwon State, Korea: a mixed-methods study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Health and nutrition problems in this rural setting may reflect individual behaviors and structural and environmental constraints. Preventive, family-based strategies targeting young and middle-aged adults are warranted. Tailored interventions integrating dietary improvement, physical activity, and local context are needed to reduce health disparities and improve community health.

item.title: An exploration of the participation experiences of university students in a social cognitive theory-based digital health behavior intervention program in Korea: a qualitative study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Pairing mobile self-monitoring with online community interaction provides valuable qualitative insights into how students experience health behavior engagement. Peer facilitation shapes a distinct contextual environment which influences user motivation, peer interaction, and social support perception. These findings offer foundational qualitative perspectives to aid in the design of potential health promotion strategies on university campuses.

item.title: Comparison of health, functional, and dietary characteristics between low-income and general income community-dwelling older adults in Korea: a cross-sectional study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Low-income older adults were more likely to have poor health status, functional limitations, oral health problems, and insufficient intake of several food groups than general income older adults. Therefore, effective interventions to improve the dietary quality of community-dwelling older adults must go beyond simple food provision and adopt an integrated approach that incorporates tailored functional support, oral health management, and sex-specific nutrition education.

item.title: Changes in hygiene management performance across monitoring visit rounds in long-term care institutions for older adults in Korea: a retrospective longitudinal observational study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Repeated hygiene and safety monitoring visits were associated with improved hygiene management performance in long-term care institutions for older adults, particularly during the early stages of repeated visits. Such field-based guidance and feedback may contribute to the strengthening of hygiene management practices in small-scale institutions.

item.title: Embedding person-centered nutrition assessment and care in Korea's Community Integrated Care for older adults and persons with disabilities: 'From Policy to Fork': a narrative review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Nutrition could function as a core operational domain of community integrated care rather than solely as nutrition education or meal delivery. Existing dietitian-led foodservice infrastructure and standard nutrition-management algorithms provide a foundation, but field-validated assessment modules, explicit accountability, service maps, and human-governed digital tools may need to be developed and evaluated. The proposed 'From Policy to Fork' framework is offered as a conceptual...

item.title: Longitudinal Mean HbA1c and Electrodiagnostic Severity of Distal Symmetric Sensorimotor Polyneuropathy in Type 2 Diabetes: Comparison With Index HbA1c
item.description: CONCLUSION: Mean HbA1c showed more consistent associations than index HbA1c across separate models, but superiority was not established. Sensitivity analyses indicated uncertainty in the ordinal association.

item.title: Energy-band alignment of stacked single-crystalline Si/α-Ga2O3p-n heterojunctions
item.description: A stacked single-crystalline Si/α-Ga(2)O(3)p-n heterojunction was formed by transferring a 100 nm p-Si nanomembrane onto anα-Ga(2)O(3)epiwafer. Theα-Ga(2)O(3)layer exhibited a (110) x-ray diffraction reflection, and the epi-layer at the Si/α-Ga(2)O(3)interface had a valence-band maximum located 4.29 ± 0.10 eV below the Fermi-level. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy depth profiling revealed decreases of 0.11 eV in the Si 2p binding energy and 0.35 eV in the Ga 3d binding energy from the bulk-like...

item.title: Multiscale Freestanding Vertically Aligned CNT Heat Sink Enabling Multimodal Heat Dissipation by Conduction, Convection, and Radiation
item.description: A vertically aligned carbon nanotube (VACNT)-based heat sink is demonstrated for passive multimodal thermal management applicable for electronic and semiconductor devices. The VACNT enables multimodal heat dissipation through axial conduction, convection facilitated by its nanoporous morphology, and radiation enabled by its superior emissivity. While conventional metallic heat sinks suffer from low surface emissivity and require complex post-processing to enhance radiative cooling, the proposed...

item.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and the Eye: Ocular Safety, Retinal Outcomes, and Clinical Implications
item.description: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists have transformed the treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, but rapidly expanding use has generated concern about ocular adverse events. In Korea, newly established national health insurance reimbursement criteria for injectable semaglutide (Ozempic prefilled pen) took effect on February 1, 2026; as use among eligible patients may expand, proportionate ophthalmic preparedness is timely. This structured narrative review evaluates randomized trials,...

item.title: Global Trends and Burden of HIV Coinfection With Extensively Drug-Resistant Tuberculosis From 1990 to 2021: The Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
item.description: CONCLUSION: Despite declines in HIV/XDR-TB burden, significant regional and demographic disparities persist, highlighting the need for targeted public health strategies in high-burden regions.

item.title: Impact of Neuromuscular Blocking Agents on Hospital Outcomes in Mechanically Ventilated Patients With Sepsis: Propensity Score Analyses of A Nationwide Sepsis Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: In patients with sepsis requiring MV, the use of NMBAs was not associated with in-hospital mortality but was linked to longer ICU stays and a higher incidence of ventilator-associated pneumonia. These findings underscore the need for cautious use of continuous NMBA infusion in this population.

item.title: Impact of Mass Resignation of Junior Doctors in Korea on Major Interventions: Interrupted Time Series Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSION: The mass resignation of junior doctors was associated with substantial and immediate reductions in healthcare service provision across multiple clinical specialties, particularly in tertiary hospitals. The absence of immediate effects for certain DPNIs likely reflects their lower reliance on junior doctors, as well as the urgency or structural characteristics of these interventions. These findings highlight the need for health policies that address unmet healthcare needs and mitigate...

item.title: Lifetime Endogenous Estrogen Exposure Predicts Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis Risk in Postmenopausal Women Based on a Nationwide Population Study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Among postmenopausal women, lifetime endogenous estrogen exposure showed a protective role from developing IPF.

item.title: Circulating Estradiol as an Independent Risk Factor for Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease and Fibrosis Risk in Women: Evidence From a Multicenter Health-Checkup Cohort
item.description: CONCLUSION: Low circulating estradiol independently increases the risk of MASLD and high-risk fibrosis in women. While its protective effect against steatosis weakens with obesity, its antifibrotic effect remains strong across all subgroups. Estradiol may serve as an important hormonal marker for risk stratification in female MASLD patients.

item.title: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Shaving With a Blade During Transoral Robotic Thyroidectomy
item.description: This video demonstrates blade-based recurrent laryngeal nerve (RLN) shaving during transoral robotic thyroidectomy in four patients with papillary thyroid carcinoma and tumor adherence to a functioning RLN. Controlled sharp dissection along the tumor-nerve interface enabled anatomical nerve preservation in all four cases, with normal vocal fold mobility at 3 months.

item.title: Association between seafood consumption and urinary bisphenol concentrations in Korean adults: findings from the Korean National Environmental Health Survey (KoNEHS 2018-2020)
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Seafood-frequency categories showed associations with spot urinary concentrations of BPA, BPF, and BPS. These cross-sectional findings do not establish a causal relationship or a specific exposure pathway. Longitudinal studies with repeated urinary measurements and more detailed assessment of seafood products, processing, and food-contact materials are needed to clarify these associations.

item.title: Dimensional crossover of thermal transport in nanoconfined liquids driven by the interplay of quasi-one-dimensional structure and wall dissipation
item.description: Heat transport in nanoconfined liquids can deviate from ordinary Fourier behavior because confinement alters liquid structure and interfacial dissipation. Although such changes may lead to quasi-one-dimensional transport or overdamped sound relaxation, the conditions under which length-dependent transport persists remain unclear. Here we use molecular dynamics simulations of monatomic liquid argon confined in carbon nanotubes with systematically varied radii and lengths. We find a...

item.title: Revealing the Atomic-Scale Structure of the Copper-Sulfuric Acid Interface
item.description: Corrosion originates from atomistic reactions occurring at dynamic solid-liquid interfaces; however, direct experimental observation of these reactions has remained elusive due to the inability to preserve transient interfacial states during characterization. To refine corrosion models, advanced techniques capable of analyzing corrosion interfaces at the atomic scale are essential. Recent advancements in cryogenic-atom probe tomography (cryo-APT) enabled 3D nanoscale analysis of frozen...

item.title: Efficacy of ORM-12741 on agitation/aggression symptoms in participants with Alzheimer's disease
item.description: INTRODUCTION: ORM-12741 is a potent and selective alpha-2C adrenoceptor antagonist. The primary objective of this study was to evaluate the efficacy of ORM-12741 in treating agitation/aggression symptoms in patients with Alzheimer's disease (AD).

item.title: Development of oxygen-releasing PVA hydrogels for protecting pancreatic beta cells from the hypoxic damage in diabetes
item.description: Hypoxia during the early post-transplantation period remains a major challenge for pancreatic β-cell survival and function before adequate vascularization is established. In this study, multilayered oxygen-generating hydrogels were developed using physically crosslinked poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) incorporating calcium peroxide (CPO) to support pancreatic β-cells under hypoxic conditions. The hydrogels were fabricated through repeated freeze-thaw cycles, with a CPO-containing core positioned...

item.title: The Need for Clinician Communication Strategies for Eating Disorders/Insulin Restriction in Type 1 Diabetes
item.description: Disordered eating behaviors occur more frequently in people with type 1 diabetes (T1D). Having T1D and eating disorders (T1DE) more than triples the risk of diabetic ketoacidosis and death compared to those without eating disorders. Insulin restriction involves purposely under-dosing or omitting insulin to lose weight. The primary objective was to identify the unique obstacles faced by diabetes healthcare clinicians (HCs) in their communication with patients who have suspected T1DE/insulin...

item.title: Evolving priorities in the WHO Bacterial Priority Pathogens List
item.description: The 2024 World Health Organization (WHO) Bacterial Priority Pathogens List (BPPL) updates the 2017 framework by expanding to 24 pathogens across 15 bacterial families, addressing the growing antimicrobial resistance (AMR) crisis, which was estimated to have caused 1.27 million deaths in 2019. The revised list introduces four new pathogen-antibiotic combinations-rifampicin-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis, macrolide-resistant Group A Streptococci, macrolide-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae,...

item.title: Tirzepatide for Severe Obesity in Adolescents Without Diabetes
item.description: CONCLUSION: This series highlights substantial weight reduction among adolescents with severe obesity treated with tirzepatide. Participants tolerated therapy during observed follow-up without reported gastrointestinal adverse effects, supporting further investigation in pediatric populations.

item.title: Direct solvothermal growth of morphology-controlled TaS<sub>2</sub> on substrates enables stable self-supported hydrogen evolution electrocatalysts
item.description: Layered transition metal dichalcogenides represent a class of materials with promising electronic properties and emerging applications as electrocatalysts for the hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). However, their preparation relies on vapor-phase and solid-state methods, while solution-phase synthesis remains challenging and underdeveloped. Here, a solvothermal route is demonstrated for the direct growth of TaS(2) on different substrates. The reaction between TaCl(5) and 1-dodecanethiol in...

item.title: Excessive censoring degrades individual-specific cortical parcellations and personalized TMS targets
item.description: Head motion systematically biases functional connectivity (FC) estimates in resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI). A common mitigation strategy is to censor high-motion volumes and discard high-motion runs. However, overly stringent censoring risks discarding signal alongside noise, potentially degrading FC estimates. Here, we test the efficacy of various censoring strategies on individual-specific cortical parcellations and personalized transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) target selection....

item.title: Three-Dimensional Gait Analysis in STXBP1-Related Disorder
item.description: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: STXBP1-related disorder (STXBP1-RD), caused by pathogenic variants in the STXBP1 gene, is a rare neurodevelopmental condition, characterized by early-onset seizures, developmental delay, intellectual disability (ID), and prominent motor dysfunction. Despite the high prevalence of motor symptoms, systematic gait characterization remains limited. The aim of this study was therefore to quantitatively assess gait in participants with STXBP1-RD.

item.title: Plasma CD55 and HIV RNA load in newly diagnosed antiretroviral therapy-naive adults: an exploratory hospital-based case-control study
item.description: CONCLUSION: Untreated HIV infection was accompanied by differences in plasma complement activation fragments and regulatory proteins. The CD55-HIV RNA load association was not supported consistently across analyses and requires independent validation.

item.title: Molecular and morphological evidence reveals four new species of the genus Lepiota (Agaricales, Verrucosporaceae) in Hebei Province, China
item.description: Four new species of Lepiota collected from Hebei Province, northern China, namely Lepiota huangyangshanensis, L. maojingbaensis, L. varia, and L. xiaowutaishanensis, are described based on morphological characteristics and molecular data. Lepiota huangyangshanensis is characterized by a cream to straw-yellow pileus with olivaceous buff to straw-yellow squamules, small ellipsoid to amygdaliform basidiospores, narrowly clavate to clavate cheilocystidia, and pileus and stipe coverings composed of...

item.title: Pyequate: A Python Package for Test Equating
item.description: Test equating adjusts scores across alternate forms of a test so that they may be used interchangeably, and is a routine requirement of any testing program that administers more than one form. Software for equating is well established in R and in standalone programs. There is no current native option in Python, despite its role as the working environment for a growing share of assessment data and downstream modeling. Analysts working in Python must therefore leave their pipeline or reimplement...

item.title: Bilirubin metabolism-related genetic variants in neonatal hyperbilirubinemia: a multicenter case-control study in northern China
item.description: Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia (NHB) is common in neonates, and genetic factors are important contributors to bilirubin metabolism. However, data on NHB-related genetic variants in northern China remain limited. This multicenter case-control study included 413 neonates hospitalized with unexplained NHB and 120 control neonates who had not been diagnosed with hyperbilirubinemia at enrollment on the day of birth. Twelve hotspot loci in UGT1A1, G6PD, SLC25A13, SLC10A1, and ABCC2 were genotyped using...

item.title: Repeat Interferon γ Release Assay Use in US Community Healthcare Organizations
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Approximately 1 in 7 individuals with positive IGRA results had repeat testing. Most repeat tests were probably not indicated according to our utilization classification, whereas nearly half of individuals without a repeat test may have benefited from one.

item.title: Sex-related refractive disparities in school-aged children: a population-based cross-sectional study of 4.47 million screening records
item.description: CONCLUSION: This study reveals distinct sex-related disparities in refractive status across childhood, observed in cross-sectional group-level comparisons. These group-level patterns may reflect developmental influences and potential cohort-related effects from differing historical exposures. These findings underscore the necessity of incorporating sex as a stratification factor in public health strategies. Implementing earlier and more intensive screening protocols for girls is crucial for...

item.title: Adhesive small bowel obstruction in a 3-year-old child with history of necrotizing enterocolitis: a case report
item.description: CONCLUSION: Children with prior intestinal surgery can present with acute abdominal pain that mimics non-surgical conditions such as mesenteric adenitis and constipation while having a complete adhesive small bowel obstruction requiring emergent surgery. Normal or equivocal ultrasound findings do not exclude this diagnosis, and a low threshold for CT is essential. Postoperative fever in such patients warrants a broad infectious workup, as multiple concurrent pathogens may coexist.

item.title: Advanced Nanoemulsion Architectures for Precision Theranostics and Next-Generation Biomedical Translation
item.description: Nanoemulsions (NEs) are kinetically stable, thermodynamically unstable colloidal systems composed of nanoscale oil and aqueous domains stabilized primarily by surfactants and, where required, co-surfactants. Their small droplet size, large interfacial area, and tunable physicochemical properties provide opportunities to improve the solubilization, dispersion, permeation, stability, and bioavailability of poorly water-soluble and labile therapeutic agents. This review provides a comprehensive...

item.title: Brain network-driven predictive neural markers for suicide risk
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: These findings highlight critical brain regions and network interactions, advancing our understanding of the neural mechanisms underlying suicide risk. Leveraging electrophysiological connectivity and innovative tools may help develop targeted interventions and early identification strategies for those at heightened risk of suicide.

item.title: Whole-genome sequencing-driven source tracing of foodborne diseases: from cgMLST/SNP typing toward an integrated framework of pan-genomics and machine learning
item.description: Core-genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) and core-genome single-nucleotide polymorphism (cgSNP) analysis have made whole-genome sequencing (WGS) the standard tool for foodborne disease surveillance. Fixed-threshold clustering is increasingly unreliable for highly clonal lineages such as Salmonella Enteritidis ST11 and Escherichia coli ST131, whose core genomes differ by only a handful of alleles even between unrelated strains. The central question is whether surveillance should keep...

item.title: Beyond disease counts: multimorbidity patterns and self-rated health in South African adults-a network analysis of the 2016 demographic and health survey
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Network analysis revealed robust disease clustering, most notably a stable infectious cluster, and subgroup-specific patterns relevant to integrated care planning. Individual-level network measures did not outperform a simple disease count. Disease counts remain a pragmatic risk marker; pattern-based measures merit prospective evaluation before clinical adoption.

item.title: Insect - fungus interactions: diversity, ecology, and applications
item.description: The coevolution of insects and fungi over more than 400 million years has produced a remarkable diversity of ecological associations, spanning obligate mutualisms to antagonistic parasitism. This systematic review synthesizes current knowledge of insect-fungus interactions by integrating ecological, evolutionary, and applied perspectives through a structured literature synthesis and network analysis of documented associations. Multiple independent evolutionary origins of insect-fungus mutualism...

item.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma: spatial immune ecosystems, metabolic remodeling, and immunotherapeutic implications
item.description: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA) is an aggressive liver malignancy characterized by pronounced cellular, spatial, and metabolic heterogeneity. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics (ST) are beginning to resolve this complexity by linking malignant, immune, stromal, and metabolic states to their tissue context. This review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial studies of iCCA across four spatial contexts: adaptive immune regions containing tertiary lymphoid...

item.title: Global impact and cost-effectiveness of tuberculosis interventions
item.description: While a range of interventions exists for tuberculosis (TB), their potential impact and cost-effectiveness are seldom directly compared across settings with different TB epidemiologies and structural drivers. Here we calibrated a deterministic TB model to epidemiological indicators from Brazil, India and South Africa. We implemented seven interventions across countries focusing on prevention, screening and diagnosis and treatment, as well as prison screening (Brazil) and nutritional...

item.title: Respiratory medicine in the ICU 2026: From physiology to precision care
item.description: This annual review summarizes major advances in respiratory medicine in the intensive care unit (ICU) published in 2025, focusing on high-impact clinical and translational studies most likely to influence current practice and future research. Across the field, 2025 strengthened the evidence base for key physiological concepts while more clearly defining where physiological strategies translate into clinical benefit and where broadly applied interventions remain insufficient, reflecting an...

item.title: Comparative viral inactivation kinetics of electron beam and gamma irradiation and functional characterization of electron beam inactivated viruses
item.description: INTRODUCTION: Electron beam (eBeam) technology is increasingly being adopted in biomedical research and industry as an alternative to cobalt-60-based gamma irradiation. However, a comprehensive understanding of how eBeam energy and dose influence viral inactivation and the preservation of viral surface antigens remains limited. This study compared the inactivation kinetics of human rotavirus (RV), human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and influenza A virus (IAV) following exposure to...

item.title: Addressing benchmarking gaps in large language models for health and medicine with dynamic red-teaming
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to answer health-related questions and support healthcare workflows, yet evidence for their safety still relies heavily on static benchmarks that can rapidly become obsolete or be optimized against. Here we introduce a Dynamic, Automatic and Systematic (DAS) red-teaming audit framework that continuously stress-tests LLMs for health across four safety-critical axes: robustness, privacy, bias and hallucination. Validated against board-certified...

item.title: Renin-angiotensin system inhibitors initiation and mortality in non-proteinuric chronic kidney disease: a target trial emulation
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Initiation of RASIs may be associated with lower risks of all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in patients with nonproteinuric CKD.

item.title: Prevalence and quantification of viable Campylobacter species in retail chicken: a comparative study using viability digital polymerase chain reaction and conventional culture methods
item.description: Campylobacter is a major foodborne pathogen and a significant public health concern, frequently associated with the consumption of undercooked poultry. Although conventional microbiological culture remains the gold standard for detection, it often fails to detect bacteria in the viable but non-culturable (VBNC) state, potentially underestimating the risk to consumers. To address this limitation, we conducted a year-long epidemiological investigation of retail chicken using propidium...

item.title: Systemic inflammatory response index: a potential mediator between substance use disorder and sleep disturbance
item.description: CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that SIRI statistically mediates the relationship between SUD and sleep disturbance in a cross-sectional context, positioning it as a potential adjunctive monitoring indicator for SUD-related psychiatric management. These results offer preliminary correlational evidence for mitigating sleep disruption through anti-inflammatory approaches, warranting further longitudinal and experimental validation.

item.title: Indications and Outcomes of Thyroid Ultrasounds Obtained at Primary Care Clinics Within a Large Health System
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: A considerable proportion of TUS orders by PCPs lack guideline support, resulting in wasteful health care utilization and significant financial impact. Urgent adherence to optimal TUS indication criteria is crucial to optimize resource allocation and minimize potential patient harm from unnecessary procedures.

item.title: Treatment of vascular dementia based on neuroprotection and neural repair strategies: from pathophysiology to natural products
item.description: Vascular dementia (VaD) is a heterogeneous cognitive disorder associated with cerebrovascular pathology and persistent vascular dysfunction. Because effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited, natural products have attracted interest as potential interventions for the complex pathology of VaD. This review examines their effects from two complementary perspectives: neuroprotection and neural repair. Experimental studies indicate that natural products can influence several interconnected...

item.title: Spatiotemporal associations between the built environment and carbon emission reduction potential of shared on-demand transit
item.description: Shared on-demand transit has emerged as a promising mobility solution for reducing transport-related carbon emissions and supporting more sustainable urban environments. However, limited evidence exists on how built environment characteristics are associated with its carbon emission reduction potential across space and time. This study aimed to quantify the maximum carbon emission reduction achievable through ODT and identify the built environment factors associated with its spatial variation....

item.title: Smartwatch-Derived Biomarkers Signal Pace of Biological Aging
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: Smartwatch-derived biomarkers captured a multidomain profile of accelerated biological aging characterized by lower mobility, poorer sleep health, and elevated physiological stress. Consumer wearables can provide low-burden, real-world indicators of biological vulnerability, although longitudinal studies are needed before clinical use.

item.title: Dopaminergic System: A Potential Therapeutic Target for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's Diseases
item.description: Dopamine is a critical neurotransmitter involved in the regulation of motor control, cognition, reward processing, motivation, and neuroendocrine functions. Increasing evidence indicates that disturbances in dopaminergic neurotransmission contribute significantly to the pathogenesis of major neurodegenerative disorders, particularly Parkinson's Disease (PD) and Alzheimer's Disease (AD). item.title: Vector versus scalar beams in atmospheric turbulence: scintillation index and average received intensity
item.description: The performance of free-space optical systems is impaired by atmospheric turbulence. Recently, vector beams have been considered more robust against atmospheric turbulence than scalar beams because their orthogonally polarized components can exhibit partially uncorrelated fluctuations. However, it remains unclear whether this advantage is fundamental or depends on the specific scalar reference used for comparison. item.title: Habitual sodium intake and metabolic abnormalities in Korean adults with obesity: a cross-sectional analysis of a prospective cohort
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In Korean adults with obesity and pre-existing metabolic conditions, increasing sodium intake was not significantly associated with higher prevalence of major metabolic diseases. In exploratory sex-stratified analyses, several atherogenic lipid markers differed across sodium intake tertiles among women only. This within-women pattern should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires confirmation in future longitudinal analyses of this cohort.

item.title: Effect-site concentrations of remifentanil to suppress coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: The identified EC(50) and EC(95) values of remifentanil for suppressing coughing during emergence from general anesthesia in adults were 2.0 and 2.7 ng·mL^(-1), respectively. Patient sex and surgical type may influence the required Ce. Careful dose adjustment is recommended to avoid delayed awakening and hypoventilation, especially in cases requiring higher concentrations.

item.title: β-Cell Recovery Patterns With Initial Combination Versus Stepwise Therapy in Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes: TRIPLE-AXEL Post Hoc Analysis
item.description: CONCLUSIONS: In newly diagnosed T2DM, both treatment strategies improved β-cell function without significant between-group differences. TCT achieved this without hypoglycaemia; however, given the on-treatment assessment, physiological equivalence cannot be concluded.

item.title: Barriers and Facilitators of Fathers' Adaptation to Children with Chronic Conditions: A Mixed-Methods Systematic Review
item.description: CONCLUSION: Fathers' adaptation is shaped by interconnected multi-level factors. Healthcare providers should routinely assess fathers' psychosocial needs during pediatric clinical encounters. Recommendations to adopt inclusive communication strategies that engage both parents in care planning and to offer flexible scheduling and caregiver leave rest on low-confidence findings and are therefore provisional.
